title: Conditional Rendering with *ngIf ✅
description: Show or hide elements dynamically using Angular’s structural if directive.

slides.title: The Most Common Structural Directive 💡
slides.content:
# *ngIf

`*ngIf` is the go‑to directive for conditionally including an element in the DOM.

Syntax: `*ngIf="expression"`

* If the expression is **truthy**, the element is added to the DOM.
* If it’s **falsy**, the element is completely removed (not just hidden).

This is different from `[hidden]` – `hidden` keeps the element in the DOM but hides it visually.

quizData.question: What happens to an element with `*ngIf="false"`?

options.text: It is hidden but still in the DOM.
It is completely removed from the DOM.
It becomes invisible but still takes up space.

quizData.explanation: `*ngIf` removes the element and its subtree from the DOM when false.

slides.title: ngIf with Else Block 🔀
slides.content:
Often you want to show alternative content when the condition is false. Use `else` with a template reference. ## The `else` Syntax ```html
Welcome back!
Please log in.
 ``` * `#loggedOut` is a template reference variable pointing to the ``. * `` is not rendered by itself – it’s a blueprint used by Angular.

slides.title: Then and Else Together
slides.content: You can also use `then` and `else` to keep the template clean:
slides.codeSnippet:
<ng-container *ngIf="isLoggedIn; then loggedInTpl else loggedOutTpl"></ng-container>

<ng-template #loggedInTpl>
  Welcome back!
</ng-template>

<ng-template #loggedOutTpl>
  Please log in.
</ng-template>

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Use `<ng-container>` for Grouping Without Extra Divs

`<ng-container>` is a logical container that doesn’t add an extra DOM element. Perfect when you need to apply `*ngIf` to multiple elements without a wrapper div.

slides.title: ngIf vs hidden ⚠️
slides.content:
Use `*ngIf` when the element is expensive to create (e.g., large component subtree) and you want to completely remove it.

Use `[hidden]` when the element is already in the DOM and toggling visibility is frequent – it’s faster because no DOM manipulation occurs.

quizData.question: To show an alternative template when *ngIf is false, use the `else` keyword followed by a template ______ variable.
quizData.explanation: You use a template reference variable like `#myTemplate`.
